messages:
Sam: quick RFC follow-up re: packed QKV vs split bias/rope + dropoutless paths. proposing runtime heuristics + graceful fallback. TL;DR: prefer fused QKV for small-to-medium sequences, fall back to split path when memory/compat issues or mixed-precision mismatch.

Maria: can you share the numbers that motivated the thresholds? :eyes:

Sam: yup. microbench on A100-80GB using fp16 kernels: seq=512 bs=8 (bs*seq=4096) -> fused_qkv+fused_rope: 1.6x throughput vs split (and ~12% less GPU mem). seq=2048 bs=1 -> fused path loses 8-12% throughput and uses more temp mem due to tile buffers. quantized int8 path still prefers split for now (precision/scale handling).

Aj: interesting. are those numbers for training-like attention or causal-only inference?

Sam: causal-only (inference). we also tried cross-attn where fused_qkv isn't applicable in the same way; we fall back to separate q/k/v matmuls + streamed rope.

Nina: runtime-wise, what does "prefer" mean? first try fused kernel and if it errors, fallback? or cost-model decision at scheduling?

Sam: both. plan: cheap static heuristics at dispatch (seq_len, batch_seq, model-size tag) to pick candidate kernel. at runtime we attempt the chosen kernel and have a low-overhead probe to validate expected output shape/kv-cache layout. if probe fails or OOM-ish conditions appear, we atomically switch to fallback and tag metrics. example config draft: 

```yaml
kernel_policy:
  - name: fused_qkv
    max_seq_len: 1024
    max_batch_seq: 8192
    prefer: true
  - name: fused_qkv_without_dropout
    max_seq_len: 2048
    prefer: true
  - name: split_qkv_bias_rope
    prefer: false
  - name: quantized_split
    device_constraints: [int8_supported]
```

Sam: the idea is early-fast decision based on tags, then a fast probe that does a tiny forward of shape (1,1) to confirm kernel viability (and correct fp16 scaling) before committing for the full batch. fallback is synchronous and increments a metric so we can alert if a kernel regresses.

Maria: does probe add latency to p99? I'm worried about tail impact if we probe often.

Sam: probe only on cold code paths or when model/version first seen on a node. also when heuristic says "ambiguous" (e.g., bs*seq near threshold). afterwards we cache chosen kernel per model+version+device.

Aj: what about dropout-free inference path? removing dropout ops helps perf but we rely on the model's runtime param to skip dropout. do we need separate kernel variants or a flag?

Leo: separate binary variants blow up maintenance. prefer single kernel with runtime flag to bypass dropout math if all inputs indicate inference mode. but fused kernels that assume no dropout can avoid writing intermediate rng state and are ~5-7% faster.

Nina: edge case: some exported models have residual dropout ops baked into the graph (e.g., fused by ONNX exporter). how do we detect and still use the faster path?

Sam: add a lightweight graph/IR sanitizer at load-time to detect no-op dropout (p=0) or patterns that are effectively identity. if sanitizable, mark model tag inference_no_dropout=true. Otherwise mark requires_dropout_handling=true and pick kernel accordingly.

Aj: fallback semantics for failures: propose atomic fallback + request retry with original inputs, but we should avoid double-charging customers. implement at runtime layer: try kernel -> on failure return transient status to router -> router retries on same token budget. we need accounting hooks.

infra-bot: note: created ticket INF-8426 to add kernel_policy config to node agent.

Maria: who owns the implementation? can we break into 3 PRs: (1) kernel selector + config, (2) probe/caching + metrics, (3) sanitizer for dropout/rope patterns?

Sam: yes. propose owners: (1) Aj (selector + config), (2) Nina (probe + metrics + fallback instrumentation), (3) Leo (graph sanitizer + export compatibility). Aj/Nina to pair on accounting hooks.

Aj: ok. I'll draft the selector RFC patch and include proto for config + examples.

Nina: I'll spec the probe API and metric names: kernel_selected, kernel_probe_ok, kernel_probe_fail, kernel_fallback_count. also add a tracing span at dispatch.

Leo: I'll write sanitizer tests against a few exported models (hf/gpt2-fused-dropout, internal export). aim for non-invasive transforms.

Maria: need a canary plan: roll to small Dedicated pool + enable probe verbose logs. if kernel_fallback_count > 0.5% for 1h, auto-disable fused path.

Sam: agreed. and add automated perf regression check: if fused path p50 cost/token > baseline by 10% for 30m, revert.

Maria: perfect. timeline?

Sam: Aj will open selector PR by EOW, Nina + Leo follow in two weeks. aim for canary in 3 weeks.

Aj: :thumbsup:

Nina: noted. I'll add the metrics to the observability dashboard template.

Sam: thanks all — keeping this lightweight so ops can iterate. ping me if blockers. :rocket:
